closure_definition: Input/trigger: anonymous user opens /login or submits configured credentials. Core behavior: render the login form, validate a single configured account, create a server-side session on success, and reject invalid credentials with a readable error. Observable result: real HTTP responses expose form fields, redirect on success with a safe session cookie, and return 401 without a session cookie on failure.
acceptance_criteria: AC-UNIT-1-001: GET /login returns 200 and renders a form with username and password fields.
AC-UNIT-1-002: POST /login with the configured username and password returns 303, redirects to /, and sets a session cookie with HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax.
AC-UNIT-1-003: POST /login with an invalid password returns 401, renders a user-readable invalid credential message, keeps the login fields visible, and does not set a session cookie.
AC-UNIT-1-004: Missing configured credentials fail fast with a user-understandable configuration error in tests or startup, not with a leaked stack trace in user responses.
exclusions: Registration, password reset, multi-account management, and role-based authorization are not part of this unit.
Old login-homepage-pilot tests are not accepted as UNIT-1 completion evidence.
priority_basis: Login entry and session creation are the first observable behavior required before the protected homepage can be validated.
